name: Meenakshi Raman
headline: 73, field associate for a university ethnobotany study, Kodaikanal
title: An Unexpected Invitation
situation: On her way back from the forest, Meenakshi passes the tea stall near the temple. An old friend, Subramani, a widower who lost his wife two years ago, calls out to her. He has known her since childhood and often walks the same path. He offers to buy her a cup of tea and suggests they sit together for a while, as he does sometimes with other elders. Meenakshi enjoys his company but feels shy about being seen alone with a man. Her own daughters are married and her husband passed away ten years ago. She has never thought of companionship before, but his gentle smile makes her pause.

context.relationship_profiles:
Subramani is a childhood friend close to her late husband; they used to drink tea together at this stall. His wife died two years ago.
Her daughters phone each morning and would worry if she were seen alone with a man.
context.tendencies:
Since becoming a widow, she takes tea only with women and never sits alone with men.
With male researchers she always asks another woman to join.
context.current_state:
She has just finished her forest round, is thirsty and warm, with the plant file under her arm; no one is waiting at home.
Her knees ache a little, but she is quietly satisfied with the new plant.
context.immediate_memories:
The steam and Subramani's voice remind her of mornings when her late husband and he argued cheerfully on that bench.
Last month he waved and she took the other path.
context.reflective_memories:
She grew up seeing widows judged for sitting alone with men; her mother never left the house without a woman companion after widowhood.
During her hardest years, Subramani's wife left rice on her doorstep without a note; she still carries that gratitude.
